headline: Clemson's Ground Game Seals Road Win Over Penn State
body: Clemson escaped Beaver Stadium with a 29-23 victory on the strength of Keith Adams Jr's two touchdown runs, a display of downhill power that Penn State's defense simply could not contain. Adams finished with 43 yards on eight carries, but the efficiency of those two scoring punches proved decisive in a game where field position and momentum shifts ruled the afternoon.

Penn State's offense kept pace through the air, with quarterback Myers completing 26 of 46 attempts for 341 yards and one touchdown, while wide receiver Hinnant was a steady presence with six receptions for 96 yards. Yet the Penn State rushing attack managed only 78 yards on the day, forcing Myers to shoulder too much of the load in a game that required balance. Clemson's Cortez matched Myers in complexity, throwing for 386 yards on 25 completions but zero touchdowns, instead relying on the supporting cast to manufacture points.

The turnover-free performance from both sides meant execution and field efficiency determined the outcome. Clemson's receiving corps, led by Monroe's 130-yard haul on just five catches, stretched Penn State's secondary vertically and created throwing lanes for Cortez throughout. The visiting defense, anchored by Lofton's eight tackles and a sack, applied enough pressure in critical moments to prevent Penn State from seizing control late.
turningPoint: Adams Jr's second touchdown run in the fourth quarter came when Penn State's defense was gassed from chasing Clemson's passing plays, breaking contain and allowing the decisive rushing score.

unsungHero.name: Monroe
unsungHero.why: His 130 yards on five receptions kept Clemson's offense vertical and opened running lanes for Adams, yet the game ball goes to the back because of two goal-line carries.
